subject: paediatrics
title: Exanthematous fevers: rash patterns and key signs

steps.tx: Exanthematous fevers are childhood viral or bacterial illnesses with a skin rash. Each has a **characteristic rash timing** and a **pathognomonic sign** that examiners test repeatedly. Learn the classic sequence of the six classical childhood exanthems, then match each to its cause. Scope here covers measles, rubella, roseola, erythema infectiosum, varicella, scarlet fever, mumps and infectious mononucleosis.
steps.say: Exanthematous fevers are childhood viral or bacterial illnesses with a skin rash. Each has a characteristic rash timing and a pathognomonic sign that examiners test repeatedly. Learn the classic sequence of the childhood exanthems, then match each to its cause. This lesson covers measles, rubella, roseola, erythema infectiosum, varicella, scarlet fever, mumps and infectious mononucleosis.

steps.tx: **Koplik spots** are the pathognomonic sign of measles. They appear on the buccal mucosa opposite the lower molars, as bluish white dots surrounded by erythema, one to three days before the rash. They fade once the rash arrives. Measles rash begins behind the ears and spreads downwards over the body, with **branny desquamation** on recovery.
steps.say: Koplik spots are the pathognomonic sign of measles. They appear on the buccal mucosa opposite the lower molars, as bluish white dots surrounded by erythema, one to three days before the rash. They fade once the rash arrives. The measles rash begins behind the ears and spreads over the face, neck and body, followed by branny desquamation on recovery.

steps.tx: **Roseola infantum**, also called sixth disease, is caused by HHV-6 and affects children aged about six months to three years. High fever lasts three to four days, then the temperature falls and a pink macular rash appears on the trunk. The rash is brief and the **fever stops before the rash begins**. Nagayama spots are seen on the palate.

steps.tx: **Varicella** shows pruritic macules that become papules, then clear fluid-filled vesicles, with umbilication. Lesions appear in crops, so several stages co-exist. The most common complication in children is **secondary bacterial skin infection** with Staphylococcus aureus or group A streptococcus. Child is infectious until all lesions have crusted. Vaccinated breakthrough cases are milder.
